subsystems.name: Vulnerable public-key crypto
subsystems.role: the RSA and elliptic-curve keys that secure payments, sessions and signatures today — and that a large quantum computer running Shor's algorithm could break.
parts: RSA and ECDSA keys in servers

subsystems.name: Post-quantum key establishment
subsystems.role: replaces key exchange with lattice- or code-based schemes.

subsystems.name: Post-quantum signatures
subsystems.role: authenticates servers, documents, software and instructions.
parts: larger keys and signatures to accommodate

subsystems.name: Cryptographic inventory and policy
subsystems.role: you cannot migrate what you cannot see; tracks every algorithm and key in the estate.

subsystems.name: Hardware roots of trust
subsystems.role: keys must be generated and used inside tamper-resistant silicon.

subsystems.name: Public key infrastructure
subsystems.role: long-lived certificate authorities and trust chains must be re-issued without breaking anything.

subsystems.name: Optional quantum links
subsystems.role: for the highest-value links, quantum key distribution plus quantum random number generators supply keys no algorithm can compute.

buildSteps.title: Inventory the cryptography
buildSteps.detail: Scan servers, mainframes, network gear, terminals and third-party libraries to build a cryptographic bill of materials: which algorithm, which key length, which lifetime.

buildSteps.title: Rank by exposure
buildSteps.detail: Flag anything whose secrets must stay confidential for years, because traffic recorded today could be decrypted later once a quantum computer exists.

buildSteps.title: Choose algorithm profiles
buildSteps.detail: Adopt the NIST standards — ML-KEM for key establishment, ML-DSA or SLH-DSA for signatures — and specify hybrid modes so a break in either half is survivable.

buildSteps.title: Rebuild the transport layer
buildSteps.detail: Upgrade TLS, SSH, IPsec and messaging stacks to negotiate hybrid post-quantum key exchange, keeping classical fallback for older peers.

buildSteps.title: Re-issue the PKI
buildSteps.detail: Generate new root and intermediate certificate authorities, publish post-quantum certificates, and run old and new chains in parallel through the transition.

buildSteps.title: Update hardware
buildSteps.detail: Firmware-update or replace HSMs, payment terminals and smart cards whose chips cannot hold larger keys or run the new maths.

buildSteps.title: Migrate signing workflows
buildSteps.detail: Move code signing, document signing and payment authorisation to dual signatures so a verifier can check both old and new.

buildSteps.title: Test interoperability and performance
buildSteps.detail: Measure handshake sizes, latency and packet fragmentation — larger keys can break middleboxes — then run chaos and rollback drills.

buildSteps.title: Roll out, monitor and retire
buildSteps.detail: Turn the new algorithms on by default, watch for negotiation failures, and finally disable RSA and elliptic-curve modes.

prerequisites.why: NIST published ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in August 2024, with a code-based backup KEM selected in 2025.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum computers that break RSA and ECC
prerequisites.why: no such machine exists; the threat is the reason to migrate early, not a precondition.

prerequisites.tech: Post-quantum capable HSMs and secure chips
prerequisites.why: some modules support the new algorithms, but much installed payment and smart-card hardware cannot be upgraded in place.

prerequisites.tech: Hybrid protocol support in mainstream software
prerequisites.why: browsers and some TLS stacks ship hybrid key exchange, but mainframes, older VPNs and embedded systems lag.
most institutions still do not know every place a vulnerable key is used, including in third-party software.
migration touches every team, and misconfiguration is more likely than algorithm failure.

pathway.milestone: standards published; hybrid key exchange running in browsers and early bank pilots
pathway.unlocks: a proven, interoperable toolkit to build on.

pathway.milestone: regulators and central banks set migration deadlines, and national-security timelines push suppliers to ship post-quantum products
pathway.unlocks: procurement pressure that forces hardware vendors to update.

pathway.milestone: full production migration of public-key infrastructure, signing and payment hardware
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end quantum-resistant transactions rather than just protected web sessions.

pathway.milestone: legacy RSA and elliptic-curve modes switched off, with quantum key distribution confined to a few high-value links
pathway.unlocks: resilience against both future quantum attack and today's recorded-traffic harvesting.
